project_info.color_palette: Dark Navy, Electric Blue, White, Bright Red

main_subject.detail: A full-month French exam calendar poster with the large top title 'BAC GÉNÉRAL BAC TECHNO', dark navy calendar grid, and blue/red schedule bars marking subject exam dates across June into early July.
main_subject.style: High-contrast timetable infographic with French weekday abbreviations, structured grid system, and bold exam event labels.

items: Top Left: Large blue rounded title blocks with white words 'BAC GÉNÉRAL' and 'BAC TECHNO'.
Top Right: No extra imagery, only the continuation of the calendar header row.
Bottom Left: Dark navy grid cells with dates starting at '1 juin' and the PHILO and GRAND ORAL bars.
Bottom Right: Red schedule bars for MATHS, ORAL DE FRANÇAIS, and the final cross-month bar reaching into early July.
Center/Background: Full June calendar matrix with French weekday initials and alternating white or navy header cells.

lighting_and_atmosphere.effect: No photographic lighting, crisp high-contrast grid edges, clean bar-label legibility, and sharp saturated red-blue blocks.

prompt.generated_prompt_string: [COMBINED PROMPT]: High quality timetable infographic poster for the French Baccalauréat exam calendar. Centerpiece is a dark navy month grid labeled 'BAC GÉNÉRAL BAC TECHNO' with French weekday initials and June dates flowing into '1 juillet'. Background is a flat dark educational schedule design. Surrounding elements: blue and red subject bars labeled 'FRANÇAIS', 'MATHS', 'PHILO', 'SPÉCIALITÉS', 'GRAND ORAL', and 'ORAL DE FRANÇAIS'. Technical style: vector timetable infographic, flat digital infographic lighting, crisp grid edges, 8k resolution, highly detailed.
prompt.negative_prompt: dark, gloomy, blurry, flat 2d, low resolution, distorted text, messy typography, muted colors, black and white, ugly, deformed shapes, watermark, signature, cropped

assets.name: French exam calendar grid
assets.usage: Preserve grid geometry, weekday labels, date placements, and subject bar spans.

reference_elements.prompt_instructions: The calendar itself is the content. Keep the French month/day wording exactly. The dates shown from June into July are in the past relative to Friday, July 17, 2026, so preserve them as a fixed schedule reference rather than updating them.
